clues: This town stands on the south bank of a great river. Low hills of rock rise just south of its streets.
The summers here are hot, with lots of rain. The winters are cold, with some snow and ice.
This river town was chosen as the new state capital in 1821. That was the same year its state joined the Union as the 24th state.
This town bears the name of the third chief of the land. He was the main hand who wrote the great paper that set the land free.
The governor of Missouri works in this town by the river. The men and women who make the laws meet in the domed capitol here.
